baseline.method: Load exact candidate adapter from git show, existing _day_bundle fixture at 1375/6000/1349 rows, one real-size day per source. Local wall includes parse/hash/raw cache; read_budget uses deterministic serial 50ms raw-read cost (not measured hosted latency). The original additive-clock stress transport serializes cost across concurrent calls; it is an aggregate serialized-service model, not an overlap-aware latency measurement. The later exact-candidate ordered benchmark below uses shared start/finish times with real overlapping threads and recorded row/raw JSON shape.
diagnosis: The 3ed0ea555 candidate already overlaps newest price-session reads four at a time. Its newest counts 260/308 cannot be limited by max_records=1000; they are consistent with a shared read deadline and expensive reads, but worker cannot prove hosted latency or why persisted continuation stalled without hosted access.

Fast local transport first pulls hit max_records=1000/1000/500. Serialized-service 50ms raw-read stress hits the 15-second operation budget at 300 rows. These are synthetic profiles, not hosted timings.

The exact candidate ordered sweep reads raw serially and never emits continuation_pending for history/T86. The 600/86400-second cadence therefore binds aggregate throughput after each successful capped pull.

T86 evidence URL-only dedupe also keeps the first prefix record/run identity. A real controller regression reproduced record_run_mismatch on the second completed pull; verified native market item dedupe fixes it without weakening terminal validation.
The ordered path mapped all bundle rows even when only a capped raw window was verified. It now constructs only the verified window while deriving partial cursors from full declared item coverage.

Controller ranking now reads scalar metadata without allocating record/metadata mappings for every historical row, retaining the original UTC ISO timestamp ordering. Registry-only snapshots without fetch bindings remain readable.
At 500 rows/day T86 needs 1317 pulls for 488*1349 rows, making the previous daily cadence incompatible with 48 hours.
The 15-second read budget, one scheduled pull per controller request, record caps and controller timeout remain unchanged. Upstream exchange request policy is unchanged.

A profiler on a native 769-row market batch measured 8.099s in distillation admission, including 3.027s in repeated SQLite connection setup/teardown. Ingest now reuses one context-local connection for that batch while preserving every existing FULL-synchronous per-record transaction, identity check, commit and rollback.

scaled_sweeps.method: Two per-date historical bundles under bundles/<source>/2026-11-11/backfill-YYYY-MM-DD/ plus a newest close per source. Real-size row counts and recorded raw JSON structure; actual adapter/hash/PIT/cursor/durable sidecars; 270ms overlap-aware receive model with real joined reader threads. Each source finishes all sample dates without gaps. No hosted claim.
scaled_sweeps.formula: For each source: 2*(cold newest startup modeled time + wall + 1s pauses) + (ordered modeled time + wall + 1s pauses)/measured ordered rows * 488*daily_rows. Sum all three sources sharing one controller slot, then add 600s worst-phase admission delay. Startup mixed-history work is charged conservatively and ordered newest replay remains included.
scaled_sweeps.assertion: The combined shared-slot sum, not just each separate source, must be below 48h.

controller_history.method: Real controller tick -> real reconcile definitions -> HTTP TestClient handlers -> scheduler/native verified adapter -> real raw/normalized/evidence/ledger/receipt stores -> terminal readback. One full 6000-row TPEx historical day plus a cold latest row on each exchange. All API/readback/persistence wall time plus 270ms transport model and 1s pauses included. Each entire tick must fit 30s. The historical partition has exactly 6000 distinct source IDs.
controller_history.formula: sample_seconds * (488*(1375+6000+1349))/6000 + 600. Apply the measured TPEx end-to-end per-row cost to all three source row totals; TPEx is the largest manifest. Separate T86 cardinality/cap and latest session cases also run.
